citations.narrative:
On 28 March 2024, an unlocked door to an enclosure housing 17 pigtailed macaques allowed animals to escape their
primary enclosure. An unknown number of macaques were found in the secondary containment bay and made contact
with the adjacent group of animals through the enclosure’s mesh. Facility staff responded to the event after hearing
animal vocalizations and were able to separate and contain the escaped macaques.
It was observed that 8 of the macaques had visible injuries that required treatment, including 3 that required surgical
repair of lacerations. One of the macaques had age-related complications in healing from injuries sustained and humane
euthanasia was elected after approximately 4 months of treatment.
It was determined that a lock on one of the primary enclosure doors was not properly secured after cage change allowing
the macaques to exit their primary enclosure. Changes in lock type, lock placement when not in use and double-checking
procedures during shifting of animals has resulted in zero reports of animal escapes at Site 002 since the event.
Visual ambiguity in lock engagement design for primary enclosures may contribute to situations allowing nonhuman
primates to escape and injure themselves and others. Primary enclosures must be designed, constructed and maintained
so that they protect the animals from injury, contain the nonhuman primates securely, and prevent accidental opening of
the enclosure, including opening by the animal. Corrected prior to inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
